texts: On day 396 of Year 2, Coraline Ash wrote in her log that a bright lantern draws a crowd of nightmoths.
Coraline Ash wrote in her log that a crowd of nightmoths brings sky-cats down from the cliff-spires.
Coraline Ash wrote in her log that sky-cats molt during hunts.
Coraline Ash wrote in her log that ground feathers make the Sunken Cove safe.
Coraline Ash read the note to Pell at breakfast.

q1_issues.issue: The sealed rule for "sky-cats molt during hunts" adds (Agent (sk_hunt $x) $x), asserting the sky-cats are the hunters, which the bare "during hunts" adjunct never states -- an event-noun that is only a temporal anchor gets its class atom and the ordering relation and nothing else.

"brings sky-cats down from the cliff-spires" drops the particle/direction "down" with no trace: the phrasal-verb rule would keep bring_down as one surface symbol, and no oblique records the downward path.

The definite plural "the cliff-spires" keeps its typing atom (GroupOf sk_cliffspire_1 cliff_spire) inside the Theme seal, although a definite referent inside a seal is presupposed and its typing should be emitted at top level beside the wrapper.

q2_gaps: meal-name temporal adjunct ("at breakfast") -- it is neither a calendar/clock term, a listed deictic, nor a listed day-part (morning/afternoon/evening/night/dawn/noon/dusk), so there is no stated licensed Time filler for it
review.notes: (Location sk_write_N sk_log_1) for "wrote in her log" is arguable -- the instruction set routes a non-spatial "in <medium>" (its own "in a statement" case) to the preposition-named In oblique instead. The rest follows doctrine: four separate non-factive write seals, indefinites kept sealed, and the Sunken Cove's Name/Member plus the compound genus atoms correctly projected to top level.

issues.reason: Time states that an event-noun serving only as a temporal anchor in an adjunct "gets its class atom and the ordering relation and nothing else", so (Agent (sk_hunt $x) $x) makes each sky-cat the hunter on words the bare "during hunts" never supplies (Core patterns: point at the words that put the atom there).

The first half stands -- "down" leaves no trace and the phrasal-verb rule ("do not split off or drop the particle") would have kept bring_down -- but the second half does not: a "from" PP answering whence is correctly Source, no oblique can carry a bare directional adverb (a preposition-named oblique needs an object NP and Manner is barred), so nothing emitted is false or ill-typed.

Core patterns (Sealing) projects a definite referent's typing to top level "in every sealing construct alike", and its worked denial case names the "GroupOf / Member typing" of a definite plural specifically, so (GroupOf sk_cliffspire_1 cliff_spire) for "the cliff-spires" belongs beside the Theme wrapper, not inside it.

gaps_confirmed: meal-name temporal adjunct ("at breakfast"): a meal noun is also an event noun, and the two routes that could take it both stop short -- it is not among the day-part constants (morning/afternoon/evening/night/dawn/noon/dusk) that the Time-point rule enumerates, and the event-noun-anchor route supplies no head for "at" (only before/after/during)
new_gaps: a directional particle separated from its verb by the object ("brings sky-cats down from the cliff-spires"): when the "from" PP already takes Source, nothing carries the bare "down" -- Manner is barred for non-manner adverbs and preposition-named obliques need an object NP -- and the phrasal-verb rule does not say whether it still applies when the particle is separated, so a licensed form must either fuse bring_down or lose the direction

seal projection for a definite PLURAL: the interim projection table lists only "Member/Name typing" as projecting out of an attitude / quotation / AccordingTo seal, while the parallel denial bullet names GroupOf as well -- the table should state that a definite plural's GroupOf projects too

non-Gregorian day-of-year dating ("on day 396 of Year 2"): (Day n) is the day-of-month granularity term and 396 cannot be one, so the day index is stored in a slot that does not mean what the text states
adjudication.defect_summary: The sealed rule for "sky-cats molt during hunts" should keep only (Member (sk_hunt $x) hunt) plus (During (sk_molt $x) (sk_hunt $x)) and drop (Agent (sk_hunt $x) $x); (GroupOf sk_cliffspire_1 cliff_spire) should be emitted at top level beside w2's Theme wrapper with the rest of P left sealed; for the lost "down" the only form that retains it is the fused particle symbol bring_down (Theme and Source unchanged), and if the separated particle is instead read as a bare directional adverb the instruction set licenses no carrier at all -- filed as a gap.
adjudication.notes: Unfiled by the reviewer but worth fixing on re-parse: (Location sk_write_N sk_log_1) for "wrote in her log" should be the preposition-named (In sk_write_N sk_log_1) -- the instruction set routes the non-spatial "in a statement" case there explicitly, and a log is a medium, not a place. Otherwise the four separate non-factive write seals, the sealed indefinites, the adjectivally-restricted distributing rule for "ground feathers", and the projected Name/Member and compound-genus atoms all follow doctrine.
